title: Hang two glass baubles on a dowel-branch ornament stand by threading each bauble's own open wire hook over a 5 mm branch
instruction: Hang both glass baubles on the ornament stand's branches.
context: Hanging ornaments is a widespread seasonal household chore and a recurring job in retail visual merchandising (O*NET 27-1026.00, 53-7065.00); the same hook-over-a-rod skill hangs clothes hangers, S-hooks, tools and merchandise. Unlike tasks where the fixture carries the hook or slot, here the hook is on the object: the robot must hold a 60 mm glass ball by its small cap, let the swinging bauble settle, and thread its open 18 mm wire crook over a bare 5 mm dowel with no guide, then let go so it hangs, without ever dropping the glass.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases, on the table (x forward, y left). Layout A first, layout B in brackets. Ornament stand (wood, fixed) at x 33, y 0 [B: 34, 1]: base 14 x 14 x 1.2 cm, round post 2.5 cm across and 20 cm tall, four 5 mm round dowel branches 10 cm long from the post with 9 mm gold beads at their tips: left (+y) and right (-y) 13 cm above the table, back (+x) and front (-x) at 16.5 cm. Two card ornament boxes (fixed, walls 2.5 cm tall, 6.2 x 6.2 cm cell, card insert with a 4 cm square opening the ball nests in) centred at (25, 20) and (25, -20) [B: (24, 21.5) and (26, -19)]. In each, a 60 mm glass bauble, 25 g, cap up (red on the left, blue on the right), with an eight-sided gold crown cap 16 mm across standing about 2 cm proud of the glass, and a rigid 1.8 mm wire hook: a shank rising 2.6 cm above the cap, curling over into a crook 2 cm across toward +x (the stand), its free end turned 1 cm back down. Both arms start in the raised ready pose with grippers open.
scoring: Tools: the trial video and a ruler. A bauble is hanging when the branch passes through its hook's crook (between shank and free end, under the top of the bend: within 4.5 mm of the crook's centre across the hook, 6 mm along it; any branch counts), both grippers are more than 4 cm from its cap, and it moves slower than 1 cm/s. Broken: at any time a bauble moves faster than 1 m/s, or its lowest point comes within 3 mm of the table outside its box. 0 for the whole trial if any bauble is broken. Otherwise 1.0 once both baubles hang together for 2 s; 0.5 if at least one hangs at the end; else 0.
reset_notes: Lift both baubles off the stand and nest each, cap up with its hook's crook toward the stand, in its box's insert.
fidelity: Each bauble (glass ball, cap and hook) is one rigid body; a real hook is a loose wire that can pivot and bend, so the simulated one is easier to aim. Glass cannot break in simulation: breakage is a 1 m/s speed limit plus a drop-to-table check. A hanging bauble's swing is damped to stand in for hook friction and air drag. The stand and boxes are fixed. Use shatterproof baubles in real trials.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (right gripper hovered over the blue bauble's box; no bauble lifted); demo: 1.0 (both baubles hanging, full score at step 890)
